rows.abstract: "Philippine Citizenship Retention Law of 2000". rows.abstract: This bill seeks to lower the age for compulsory and optional retirement of private sector employees from sixty- five (65) to fifty-five (55) and from sixty (60) to fifty (50) years, respectively. It also seeks to change the name of Social Security System (SSS) into the Social Security Insurance System (SSIS). Said measure likewise aims to expand the benefits given to private sector employees, which shall include life insurance benefits, in the event of their retirement thus further amending forthe purpose Republic Act No. 8282, otherwise known as the Social Security Act of 1997.

rows.abstract: The bill seeks to subject foreign offenders to the provisions of the Revised Penal Code, and prosecute them for crimes under the said Code as well as those defined by special laws if they are arrested while in Philippine territory.

rows.author: A034
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE BARANGAY CHAIRMAN OR PUNONG BARANGAY TO EXECUTE OR TO AID IN THE EXECUTION OF WARRANT OF ARREST AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any provision of law to the contrary notwithstanding , any duly elected Barangay Chairman or Punong Barangay is hereby authorized to execute and serve warrants of arrest issued by the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, Sandiganbayan, Regional Trial courtsm Netropolitan Trial Courts, Municipal Trial Courts and Metropolitan Circuit Trial Courts in the manner provided hereinafter, and within his area of jurisdiction without prejudice to the execution and service of such warrants of arrest by all other law enforcement agencies and officers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2000-05-17

rows.author: A034
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE THE AUTHORITY TO SETTLE MINOR CRIMINAL OFFENSES
rows.abstract: the Deaprtment of Justice (DOJ) through the Office of the Chief State Prosecutor shall have the authority to bring together the parties before them and settle their cases, provided that the subject criminal offenses are minor in character as hereinafter defined. "Minor criminal offenses" shall mean those offenses punishable by imprisonment not exceeding one (1) year and or a fine not exceeding five thousand pesos (P5,000).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2000-05-17

rows.author: A034
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPOSE CRIMINAL LIABILITY UPON PUBLIC OFFICERS WHO MALICIOUSLY OR NEGLIGENTLY FAIL TO TESTIFY IN COURT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 208 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: THE PENALTY OF PRISON CORRECCIONAL IN ITS MAXIMUM PERIOD AND PERPETUAL OR TEMPORARY SPECIAL DISQUALIFICATIO N TO HOLD PUBLIC OFFICE SHALL BE IMPOSED UPON ANY PUBLIC OFFICER OR OFFICER OF THE LAW, WHO, IN DERELICTION OF THE DUTIES OF HIS OFFICE, SHALL MALICIOUSLY OR NEGLIGENTLY FAIL TO TESTIFY IN COURT, AFTER HAVING BEEN DULY SERVED WITH A SUBPOENA, THEREBY RESULTING TO THE DISMISSAL OF THE CASE.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12305
